prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1499; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver following a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Insured reports a minor front-end impact and states the other vehicle's driver is also reporting neck and back discomfort. Claimant has not retained counsel at this time. Assigned to field adjuster for vehicle inspection and statement collection.

Entry 2: Recorded statement obtained from claimant. Claimant describes stopping in traffic when the other vehicle crossed the centerline at low speed. Reports stiffness in the neck and lower back the following morning. Claimant indicated they have seen a primary care provider and are awaiting follow-up. No attorney involved. Advised claimant of the process for submitting medical records.

Entry 3: Photos of both vehicles reviewed. Bumper cover and radiator support damage noted on the claimant's vehicle, consistent with a low-speed frontal impact. Airbag did not deploy. Estimate requested from the body shop and will be compared against the initial appraisal.

Entry 4: Medical records received from the claimant's provider. Diagnosis listed as cervical and lumbar strain with muscle spasm. Treatment plan includes physical therapy and anti-inflammatory medication. Records reviewed and forwarded to the bodily injury evaluation queue. Claimant remains unrepresented and has been sent a written explanation of benefits.

Entry 5: Follow-up call placed to claimant to confirm receipt of the written explanation and to check on therapy attendance. Claimant reports symptoms are improving and expects to complete the current treatment plan. File remains open pending final medical report and repair invoice.
